morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 heifer 是不可再按常用词缀拆解的单纯词，不能分析为 heif + -er。复数：heifers；专业派生词：heifer + -ette → heiferette，指体型和发育程度接近成年母牛的大型小母牛；没有庞大的常用派生词族。[heiferette 释义来源：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/heiferette) CEFR-C2 为编辑难度估级；未核实的考试归属不列入标签。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, heifer is a simple lexical base, not heif + the agent suffix -er. Its plural is heifers; the specialized derivative heifer + -ette → heiferette denotes a large heifer approaching a mature cow in size and development; there is no extensive common derivative family. [Heiferette definition: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/heiferette) CEFR-C2 is an editorial difficulty estimate; unverified examination affiliations are omitted.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: young cow（年轻母牛）是较宽泛的近义表达；cow（母牛）通常指成年母牛，畜牧语境中常指已产犊者；female calf（雌性牛犊）强调幼龄。heifer 特别突出年轻母牛及通常尚未产犊的身份。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Young cow is a broader near-equivalent; cow usually denotes an adult female and often one that has calved in farming contexts; female calf emphasizes infancy. Heifer specifically identifies a young female, usually before her first calving.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 按牛的成长阶段记：雌性牛犊 → heifer（年轻、通常未产犊的母牛）→ 已产犊的成年母牛。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the life stage: female calf → heifer, a young female usually before first calving → mature cow that has calved.

etymology_story.zh: requisition 在中古英语时期经中古法语或中世纪拉丁语传入，最终源于拉丁语 requīrere（寻找、要求）的相关名词。它从正式要求发展出物资申领和官方征用等意义，随后也用作动词。[来源：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/requisition)
etymology_story.en: Requisition entered Middle English through French or Medieval Latin, ultimately from a noun related to Latin requīrere, meaning to seek or require. Its official-demand meaning developed into administrative requests and compulsory provision, with later use as a verb. [Source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/requisition)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词以 requisition 为完整词基，名词转动词不改变拼写或重音；不宜机械拆成 re-（再次）+ 一个独立英语词。派生：requisition + -er → requisitioner（申领人）；requisition + -ing → requisitioning（申领或征用这一行为）；requisition + -ed → requisitioned（已申领的；已征用的）。相关同源词有 require（要求）、requirement（要求；所需之物）、requisite（必需的；必需品）。CEFR-C2 为编辑难度估级；未核实的考试归属不列入标签。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern morphology treats requisition as a whole base; conversion from noun to verb changes neither spelling nor stress. It should not be mechanically interpreted as re-, meaning again, plus an independent English word. Forms include requisitioner, a person making a requisition; requisitioning, the activity; and requisitioned, requested or taken officially. Related words are require, requirement, and requisite. CEFR-C2 is an editorial difficulty estimate; unverified examination affiliations are omitted.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: request（请求）较中性，不必经过正式程序；demand（要求）突出强硬语气或权利主张；commandeer（征用）突出凭权力接管物品。requisition 兼有制度化申领和官方征用两类用法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Request is neutral and need not involve formal procedures; demand emphasizes insistence or a claimed right; commandeer emphasizes taking control through authority. Requisition covers both procedural requests and official compulsory provision.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把“需要”写进正式程序：交单就是申领，凭官方权力调取就是征用。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Put a need through an official channel: a submitted form requests supplies; an authoritative order requisitions property.

morphology_enriched.zh: bookmaker 截短为 book-，再加口语称呼后缀 -ie → bookie；复数为 bookies，另有拼写变体 booky。相关词族：bookmaker（赌注经纪人）、bookmaking（接受投注的业务）。bookie 本身没有常用的动词或副词派生。CEFR-C2 为编辑难度估级；未核实的考试归属不列入标签。
morphology_enriched.en: Bookmaker is clipped to book- and combined with the familiar suffix -ie to form bookie; the plural is bookies, and booky is a spelling variant. Related family members are bookmaker, the betting operator, and bookmaking, the business of accepting bets. Bookie has no common derived verb or adverb. CEFR-C2 is an editorial difficulty estimate; unverified examination affiliations are omitted.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bookmaker（赌注经纪人）是较中性的完整形式；betting operator（博彩经营者）偏商业或监管语体，可指公司；turf accountant（赛马赌注经纪人）是英式传统委婉说法。bookie 更口语化，本身并不必然表示非法经营者。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bookmaker is the neutral full form; betting operator is a business or regulatory term that can denote a company; turf accountant is a traditional British euphemism. Bookie is more informal and does not inherently mean an illegal operator.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: book 是记赌注的账簿：管这本投注账的人，就是 bookie。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a book recording bets: the person running that betting book is the bookie.

etymology_story.zh: erstwhile 由表示“从前”的 erst 和表示时间的 while 组合而成，最初用作副词，两部分都有古英语渊源。表示“昔日的”的形容词用法出现较晚，如今比副词用法常见。[来源：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/erstwhile)
etymology_story.en: Erstwhile combines erst, meaning formerly, with the temporal word while, both with Old English ancestry, and first functioned as an adverb. Its later adjective use, meaning former, is now more frequent. [Source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/erstwhile)

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史复合结构：erst（从前）+ while（某个时候）→ erstwhile；在现代英语中通常作为固定整体使用。形容词和副词同形同音，没有常用的比较级、最高级或后缀派生词族；相关词有古雅的 erst（从前）和 ere（在……以前），以及 while（一段时间）。CEFR-C2 为编辑难度估级；未核实的考试归属不列入标签。
morphology_enriched.en: The historical compound is erst, formerly, + while, at a time; modern English generally treats it as a fixed whole. Its adjective and adverb share spelling and pronunciation, and it has no usual comparative, superlative, or suffix-derived family. Related words include archaic erst, formerly; ere, before; and while, a period of time. CEFR-C2 is an editorial difficulty estimate; unverified examination affiliations are omitted.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: former（从前的）最中性，通常表示某种身份或关系已结束；onetime（一度的）也可修饰过去的身份，语气较不庄重；formerly（从前）是副词用法的中性对应词。erstwhile 整体更书面，有时带回顾或疏离意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Former is neutral and usually marks an ended role or relationship; onetime also describes a past identity but sounds less elevated; formerly is the neutral adverbial equivalent. Erstwhile is more literary and can suggest retrospective distance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: erst 指向过去，while 指向某个时候：合起来就是“从前”，放在名词前就是“从前的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Erst points backward and while points to a time: together they mean formerly, or former before a noun.

etymology_story.zh: theist 在十七世纪英语中出现，由源自希腊语 theos（神）的构词成分与 -ist 构成。早期用法与 deist（自然神论者）有所重叠，后来逐渐形成区别，现代广义用法指相信神存在的人。[词源来源：在线词源词典](https://www.etymonline.com/word/theist) [名词及形容词释义：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/theist)
etymology_story.en: Theist appeared in seventeenth-century English, combining an element from Greek theos, god, with -ist. Early usage overlapped with deist before the terms became more distinct; its broad modern sense is someone who believes that a god or gods exist. [Etymology: Etymonline](https://www.etymonline.com/word/theist) [Noun and adjective definitions: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/theist)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析：the-（theo- 在此词中的形式，表示“神”）+ -ist（持某种信念的人）→ theist；复数为 theists。核心词族：theism（有神论）、theistic（有神论的）、theistical（有神论的，较少见）、theistically（以有神论的方式）。扩展词族：atheist／atheism（无神论者／无神论）、monotheist／monotheism（一神论者／一神论）、polytheist／polytheism（多神论者／多神论）、antitheist／antitheism（反有神论者／反有神论）、nontheist／nontheism（非有神论者／非有神论）。CEFR-C2 为编辑难度估级；未核实的考试归属不列入标签。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is the-, the form of theo- meaning god used here, + -ist, a person holding a belief, → theist; the plural is theists. The core family includes theism, belief in a god or gods; theistic and less common theistical, relating to that belief; and theistically, in a theistic manner. Extended forms include atheist/atheism, monotheist/monotheism, polytheist/polytheism, antitheist/antitheism, and nontheist/nontheism, denoting respectively absence of belief in gods, belief in one god, belief in multiple gods, opposition to theism, and a position without theistic belief. CEFR-C2 is an editorial difficulty estimate; unverified examination affiliations are omitted.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: believer（信神者；信徒）较宽泛，具体相信什么依语境而定；deist（自然神论者）通常相信创造者，却不接受神启或神的持续干预；monotheist（一神论者）明确只相信一位神。后两者属于更具体的相关类别，不能在所有语境中与 theist 互换；形容词 theistic 通常比 theist 更常见。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Believer is broader and depends on context for the belief involved; deist usually identifies someone who accepts a creator but rejects revelation or continuing divine intervention; monotheist specifically means a believer in one god. The latter two identify narrower related categories rather than universal substitutes for theist; as an adjective, theistic is generally more usual.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: the- 表示“神”，-ist 表示“持某种信念的人”：相信神存在的人就是 theist。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The- means god and -ist marks a person holding a belief: a theist believes that a god or gods exist.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经晚期拉丁语 urethra 借入希腊语 ourēthra，后者与 ourein“排尿”有关。其名称直接指向排尿的通道。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed urethra through Late Latin from Greek ourēthra, related to ourein, meaning “to urinate.” Its name identifies the passage used in urination.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 urethra 是不可自由拆分的医学名词；词干形式为 urethr-，结合形式为 urethro-。主要词族：urethr- + -al → urethral（尿道的）；urethr- + -itis → urethritis（尿道炎）；urethro- + -scopy → urethroscopy（尿道镜检查）；urethro- + -plasty → urethroplasty（尿道成形术）；urethro- + -tomy → urethrotomy（尿道切开术）。复数为 urethras 或 urethrae。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, urethra is a medical noun without freely separable everyday components; its stem is urethr- and its combining form is urethro-. Principal family members include urethral (urethr- + -al), urethritis (urethr- + -itis), urethroscopy (urethro- + -scopy), urethroplasty (urethro- + -plasty), and urethrotomy (urethro- + -tomy). The plural is urethras or urethrae.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: urethral canal（尿道管腔）是接近的解剖学表达；urinary passage（排尿通道）是较宽泛的描述，不能在所有语境中精确替换。ureter（输尿管）不是近义词：它连接肾脏与膀胱，而 urethra 连接膀胱与体外。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Urethral canal is a close anatomical expression; urinary passage is a broader description and is not always an exact substitute. Ureter is not a synonym: it carries urine from a kidney to the bladder, whereas the urethra carries it from the bladder outside the body.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“排尿”记通道：膀胱 → urethra（尿道）→ 体外。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the historical idea of urinating with the exit route: bladder → urethra → outside.

etymology_story.zh: 该词见于中古英语，形式为 pronge，可能与低地德语中表示杆或棍的词有关，但更早来源并不确定。原指突出的尖齿，后来引申为计划或攻势中共同发挥作用的不同部分。
etymology_story.en: The word appears in Middle English as pronge and may be related to a Low German word for a pole or stick, though its earlier origin is uncertain. From a projecting point, it developed the figurative meaning of one coordinated part of a plan or attack.

morphology_enriched.zh: prong 是独立词基，名词可通过零派生用作动词。主要词族：prongs（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、pronged（动词过去式、过去分词；有叉齿的）、pronging（动词现在分词）；two-pronged（双齿的；双管齐下的）、three-pronged（三齿的；三管齐下的）、multipronged（多齿的；多方面同时进行的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Prong is a free base, and the noun also forms a verb by conversion. Principal family members are prongs, pronged, and pronging; pronged also functions adjectivally. Compounds include two-pronged, three-pronged, and multipronged, describing either physical points or coordinated lines of action.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tine（叉齿）更专指叉子或耙子的细长齿；spike（尖刺）强调尖锐的突起，不一定成组；在策略义中，strand（组成部分、线索）强调复杂整体中的一条发展线，而 prong 强调共同指向目标的行动方向。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tine more specifically names a slender tooth of a fork or rake; spike emphasizes a sharp projection that need not belong to a set. Figuratively, strand emphasizes one developing element within a complex whole, while prong emphasizes a coordinated direction of action.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一把叉子，多根尖齿；一个目标，多路推进。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One fork has several points; one strategy can advance through several prongs.

etymology_story.zh: Norse 通常被认为借自荷兰语中表示“挪威的”的形式，如旧拼写 noorsch，与表示“北”的词有关。英语中的用法后来扩展到古代斯堪的纳维亚的人群、语言和文化。
etymology_story.en: Norse is generally traced to a Dutch form meaning “Norwegian,” such as the older spelling noorsch, ultimately associated with north. English usage broadened to cover the people, language, and culture of historical Scandinavia.

morphology_enriched.zh: Norse 在现代英语中作为整体词基使用，不宜拆成 Nor- 与 -se。主要词族及复合形式：Norse + man → Norseman（古代北欧男子；复数 Norsemen）；Norse + woman → Norsewoman（古代北欧女子；复数 Norsewomen）；Old Norse（古诺尔斯语）。Norse 及这些文化、语言名称均须大写首字母。
morphology_enriched.en: Norse functions as a whole base in modern English and should not be divided into Nor- and -se. Principal related formations are Norseman, plural Norsemen; Norsewoman, plural Norsewomen; and Old Norse. Norse retains its initial capital in these cultural and linguistic uses.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Scandinavian（斯堪的纳维亚的）适用范围更广，可指现代人群与文化；Viking（维京人的）更突出维京时代的航海、劫掠与海外活动，不能涵盖所有古代北欧人；Old Norse（古诺尔斯语）是语言义中更明确的名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Scandinavian is broader and can describe modern people and culture. Viking more specifically evokes Viking Age seafaring, raiding, and overseas activity and does not encompass every Norse person. Old Norse is the more explicit name when referring to the historical language.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 由 north“北方”联想：北方古人、北欧神话、古代北欧语。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use north as the anchor: northern ancestors, northern myths, and their historical language.

senses.meaning_zh: 缺乏自信的；羞怯拘谨的
senses.meaning_en: shy and hesitant because of a lack of self-confidence
senses.english_definition: If you are diffident, you lack confidence in yourself and are hesitant about speaking or acting.
senses.collocation_en: a diffident manner; diffident about expressing an opinion
senses.collocation_zh: 羞怯拘谨的举止；不太敢表达意见

etymology_story.zh: 该词源自拉丁语 diffident-，即 diffidere“不信任”的现在分词词干，由 dis-（否定）与 fidere（信任）构成。英语中的意义逐渐集中为“不相信自己”，因而表现得羞怯、犹豫。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin diffident-, the present participial stem of diffidere, meaning “to distrust,” formed from negative dis- and fidere, “to trust.” In English, its meaning narrowed toward distrust of one's own abilities, producing shyness or hesitation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族以 diffident 为形容词词基：diffident + -ly → diffidently（羞怯地）；对应抽象名词为 diffidence（缺乏自信；羞怯）。历史上可分析为 dif-（dis- 在 f 前的变体，表示否定）+ fid（信任）+ -ent；confident（自信的）、confidence（自信）属于同源关联词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern family consists chiefly of diffident, diffidently (diffident + -ly), and the corresponding abstract noun diffidence. Historically, the structure is dif-, a form of negative dis- before f, plus fid, “trust,” and -ent. Confident and confidence are related through the same Latin root.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: shy（害羞的）着重社交场合的不自在；timid（胆怯的）更强调害怕或不敢行动；self-effacing（不愿突出自己的）强调低调退让，不一定缺乏自信。diffident 的核心是对自己的能力或判断缺少把握。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Shy emphasizes social discomfort; timid emphasizes fear or reluctance to act; self-effacing emphasizes avoiding attention and need not imply low confidence. Diffident specifically suggests uncertainty about one's own abilities or judgment.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fid＝信任；不太信任自己 → 羞怯、没把握。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fid means trust: insufficient trust in yourself produces a diffident manner.

etymology.text: 中古英语借自拉丁语 distendere，由 dis- 与 tendere“伸展”构成。把它想成内部压力把外壁向四周撑开。

senses.meaning_zh: 使胀大；因内部压力而膨胀
senses.meaning_en: to swell or cause something to swell through internal pressure
senses.english_definition: If a part of the body or another enclosed structure distends, or something distends it, it becomes larger because pressure stretches it from within.
senses.collocation_en: a distended abdomen; distended with gas
senses.collocation_zh: 胀大的腹部；因气体而胀大
senses.sentence_en: Gas can distend the stomach and cause discomfort.
senses.sentence_zh: 气体会使胃胀大，引起不适。

etymology_story.zh: 该词源自拉丁语 distendere，由 dis-（向不同方向、分开）与 tendere（伸展）组成。原本“向外撑开”的含义在英语中主要用于描述内部压力造成的胀大。
etymology_story.en: Distend comes from Latin distendere, formed from dis-, “apart,” and tendere, “to stretch.” The underlying idea of stretching outward developed into the English sense of swelling under pressure from within.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按历史词素分析为 dis-（向外、分开）+ tend（伸展）；这里的 tend 是拉丁语来源的词根，不能按日常动词 tend“照料”理解。主要词族：distends、distended（胀大的；也作过去式和过去分词）、distending；distension 或 distention（膨胀；胀大）；distensible（可胀大的）；distensibility（可扩张性）。
morphology_enriched.en: The historical components are dis-, “apart,” and tend, “stretch”; this root should not be interpreted as the everyday verb tend meaning “care for.” Principal family members include distends, distended, distending, distension or distention, distensible, and distensibility.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: swell（肿胀、增大）最宽泛，不限定成因；expand（扩大、扩张）适用于体积、范围或规模增加；inflate（充气使膨胀）通常强调气体进入。distend 特别强调内部压力把外壁撑大，常见于医学或技术描述。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Swell is the broadest term and does not specify the cause; expand can describe increases in volume, extent, or scale; inflate usually emphasizes filling with gas. Distend particularly emphasizes internal pressure stretching an enclosing wall and is common in medical or technical descriptions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dis- 向四周 + tend 伸展：里面一撑，外壁就胀。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dis- apart + tend stretch: pressure inside stretches the walls outward.

senses.meaning_zh: 节庆；尤指西班牙或拉丁美洲的宗教节日或公众庆典
senses.meaning_en: A festival or celebration, especially a religious or public celebration in Spain or Latin America.
senses.english_definition: A fiesta is a celebration, especially in Spain or Latin America, when people gather to enjoy music, dancing, food, or other festivities.
senses.collocation_en: a traditional fiesta; an annual fiesta
senses.collocation_zh: 传统节庆；一年一度的节庆
senses.sentence_en: The whole village gathers in the square for the annual fiesta.
senses.sentence_zh: 全村人聚集在广场上，参加一年一度的节庆活动。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 fiesta 借自西班牙语，最终源于拉丁语 festa，意为节日或庆典，与 festus“节庆的”有关。英语沿用了其庆祝含义，尤其用于具有西班牙或拉丁美洲文化特色的节庆。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed fiesta from Spanish, ultimately from Latin festa, meaning holidays or celebrations and related to festus, meaning festive. In English, it retains the idea of celebration, especially one associated with Spanish or Latin American culture.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 fiesta 是整体借入的独立词基，没有可供英语构词分析的常用前后缀。复数为 fiestas；fiesta-like＝fiesta＋-like，表示“像节庆的”，属于可按需构成的形容词，并非常用固定派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, fiesta is an independent borrowed base with no usual English prefix or suffix to separate. Its plural is fiestas; fiesta-like combines fiesta with -like to mean resembling a fiesta, but is a freely formed adjective rather than an established common derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: festival（节庆）适用范围最广，可指文化、艺术或宗教活动；celebration（庆祝活动）强调庆祝某件事；carnival（狂欢节）通常突出游行、盛装和街头娱乐。fiesta 尤其带有西班牙或拉丁美洲的文化色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Festival is the broadest term for cultural, artistic, or religious events; celebration emphasizes marking a particular occasion; carnival typically suggests parades, costumes, and street entertainment. Fiesta especially evokes Spanish or Latin American culture.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 fiesta 与同源的 festive“节庆的”联系起来：节庆气氛中的音乐、舞蹈和欢聚。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect fiesta with its relative festive: music, dancing, and people gathering to celebrate.

etymology.text: 英语借自德语 Phänotypus，德语名称取材于希腊语 phainein“显示”和 typos“类型”。重点是实际表现出的特征。

usage_note: phenotype 是实际表现出来的特征；genotype 是遗传组成。环境也会影响表型。

senses.meaning_zh: 表型；生物在基因与环境共同作用下表现出的可观察或可测量特征
senses.meaning_en: The observable or measurable characteristics of an organism resulting from its genes and environment.
senses.english_definition: An organism's phenotype is the set of characteristics it actually develops, such as its appearance, physiology, or behavior, through the interaction of its genes and its environment.
senses.collocation_en: an observable phenotype; a disease phenotype
senses.collocation_zh: 可观察的表型；疾病表型
senses.sentence_en: Plants with the same genotype can develop different phenotypes under different growing conditions.
senses.sentence_zh: 基因型相同的植物，在不同的生长条件下可能形成不同的表型。

senses.meaning_zh: 测定、记录或分析生物或样本的表型
senses.meaning_en: To determine, record, or analyze the phenotypic characteristics of an organism or sample.
senses.english_definition: When researchers phenotype organisms or samples, they examine or measure their characteristics to describe them or classify them into groups.
senses.collocation_en: phenotype patients; phenotype cells
senses.collocation_zh: 对患者进行表型分析；对细胞进行表型鉴定
senses.sentence_en: The researchers phenotyped the plants for drought tolerance.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员测定了这些植物的耐旱表型。

etymology_story.zh: 丹麦遗传学家威廉·约翰逊于1909年提出 phenotype 及其对应术语 genotype；英语形式对应德语 Phänotypus。其希腊语构词成分表达“显现”和“类型”，用来区分实际表现出的性状与遗传组成。
etymology_story.en: The Danish geneticist Wilhelm Johannsen introduced phenotype and its companion term genotype in 1909; the English form corresponds to German Phänotypus. Its Greek-derived elements convey appearing and type, distinguishing expressed characteristics from genetic constitution.

morphology_enriched.zh: phenotype＝pheno-（显现；可观察的表现）＋type（类型）；名词可零派生为动词。主要词族：phenotypes（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、phenotypic／phenotypical（表型的）、phenotypically（在表型上）、phenotyped（已进行表型分析的；过去式及过去分词）、phenotyping（表型测定；现在分词）、phenotyper（进行表型分析的人或设备）。
morphology_enriched.en: Phenotype combines pheno- meaning appearing or observable expression with type meaning form or category; the noun also functions as a verb through conversion. The main family includes phenotypes, phenotypic and phenotypical meaning relating to phenotype, phenotypically meaning in terms of phenotype, phenotyped, phenotyping meaning the assessment of phenotypes, and phenotyper meaning a person or device that performs such assessment.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: trait（性状）通常指某一个特征；characteristic（特征）是更宽泛的普通用词；appearance（外观）仅侧重看得见的形态。phenotype 可指整体或特定方面的表现，涵盖外观、生理和行为，并不局限于肉眼可见的特征。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Trait usually denotes an individual feature; characteristic is a broader everyday term; appearance concerns visible form. Phenotype can describe an organism's overall expression or a particular aspect of it, including physiological and behavioral features that are not directly visible.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pheno-＝显现，type＝类型：基因与环境共同作用后，实际“表现出来的样子和特性”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pheno- means appearing and type means form: the characteristics that actually emerge from genes interacting with the environment.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音符号标出重读音节。

forms: 可数名词；复数 prefixes；动词词形有 prefixed、prefixing。
family: prefixation 加前缀；prefixed 加有前缀的

morphology.text: pre-（在前）+ fix（固定）→ prefix（固定在词前的部分）。

etymology.text: 名词借自新拉丁语 praefixum，源于拉丁语 praefigere“固定在前面”。把新字母接到词首，就是前缀的直观图像。

usage_note: prefix 接在词首，suffix 接在词尾；本课只考构词中的前缀。

senses.meaning_zh: 前缀；加在词或词基前以改变意义的构词成分

senses.meaning_en: An initial element placed before a number, code, or name.
senses.english_definition: A prefix is a number, letter, or title placed before the main part of another number, code, or name to identify or qualify it.
senses.collocation_en: an international dialling prefix; a title prefix
senses.collocation_zh: 国际拨号前缀；姓名前的称号
senses.sentence_en: All temporary accounts have the prefix TEMP.

senses.meaning_zh: 在……前加上；给……添加前缀或前置内容
senses.meaning_en: To add something to the beginning of a word, name, number, or text.
senses.english_definition: If you prefix something with a letter, word, or other element, you put that element at its beginning.
senses.collocation_en: prefix a filename with a date; prefix a word with un-

senses.sentence_zh: 在每个文件名前加上日期，以便对文件进行排序。

etymology_story.zh: prefix 源于拉丁语 praefigere“固定在前面”，由 prae-“在前”与 figere“固定”组成；名词与其过去分词形式 praefixum 有关。表示“放在前面”的基本含义后来形成了语法中的“前缀”义，并扩展到号码、代码等前置标识。
etymology_story.en: Prefix comes from Latin praefigere, meaning to fasten in front, formed from prae- meaning before and figere meaning to fasten; the noun is associated with the participial form praefixum. The basic idea of placing something first developed into the grammatical sense and extended to initial elements in numbers and codes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 教学上可分析为 pre-（在前）＋fix（固定），但 prefix 的历史来源是拉丁语整体词形，并非现代英语临时拼合。主要词族：prefixes（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、prefixed（加有前缀的；过去式及过去分词）、prefixing（添加前缀；现在分词）、prefixal（前缀的）、prefixation（前缀构词法；添加前缀）。affix、suffix 与其共享历史词根，但不是 prefix 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: For learning purposes, prefix can be analyzed as pre- meaning before plus fix meaning fasten, although historically it comes from an existing Latin formation. Its main family includes prefixes, prefixed, prefixing, prefixal meaning relating to prefixes, and prefixation meaning the formation of words with prefixes or the addition of a prefix. Affix and suffix share its historical root but are not direct derivatives of prefix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: affix（词缀）是上位词，包括前缀和后缀等；prepose（前置）指把成分放在另一成分前，常用于语言学；prepend（在开头添加）常用于计算机和文本处理。prefix 强调添加在开头，也可特指构词前缀。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Affix is the broader category that includes prefixes and suffixes; prepose means to place an element before another and is often linguistic; prepend is common in computing and text processing. Prefix emphasizes adding an initial element and can specifically refer to word formation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pre-＝前，fix＝固定：固定在前面的成分就是 prefix；把它加到前面就是动词 prefix。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pre- means before and fix means fasten: a prefix is fastened at the front; to prefix is to put it there.

meaning: 代替的位置；用在 in lieu of 中表示代替

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音符号标出重读音节。

forms: 主要见固定短语 in lieu of；此用法通常没有复数。
family: lieutenant 代理者；中尉（具有历史构词联系）

morphology.text: lieu（位置）+ tenant（法语：占据者）→ lieutenant（原指代他人任职的人）；这是法语组合后借入英语的词，lieu 本身是独立词素。

etymology.text: 中古英语 liue 借自盎格鲁法语 liu、lieu，源头是拉丁语 locus“地方”。in lieu of 就像“放在另一个东西的位置上”。

usage_note: in lieu of 是较正式的“代替”，近于 instead of；不是“除此之外再加上”。

senses.pos: n. 名词（主要用于固定短语）
senses.meaning_zh: 替代的位置；in lieu of 表示“代替”，in lieu 表示“作为替代或补偿”
senses.meaning_en: Place or stead, chiefly in expressions meaning instead of or as a substitute.
senses.english_definition: If something is provided in lieu of something else, or simply in lieu, it is provided instead of that other thing or as compensation for it.
senses.collocation_en: payment in lieu of notice; time off in lieu
senses.collocation_zh: 代通知金；补休
senses.sentence_en: She received an extra day's leave in lieu of payment for the overtime.
senses.sentence_zh: 她获得了一天额外假期，作为加班费的替代补偿。

etymology_story.zh: lieu 经盎格鲁法语和古法语中表示“地方”的词形进入中古英语，最终源于拉丁语 locus“地方”。in lieu of 保留了“处在另一事物的位置上”的原始空间意象，由此表示“代替”。
etymology_story.en: Lieu entered Middle English through Anglo-French and Old French forms meaning place, ultimately from Latin locus. In lieu of preserves the spatial image of occupying another thing's place and therefore means instead of.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 lieu 是不可进一步拆分的借入词基，通常不单独使用，也没有常用的生产性派生词族。核心形式是 in lieu of（代替）和 in lieu（作为替代或补偿）；lieutenant 在法语历史构词上由 lieu“位置”与 tenant“占据者”组成，但不是现代英语用 lieu 派生出的词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, lieu is an unanalyzable borrowed base, normally restricted to set expressions and without a common productive derivative family. Its central expressions are in lieu of meaning instead of and in lieu meaning as a substitute or compensation. Lieutenant historically combines French lieu meaning place with tenant meaning holder, but is not a modern English derivative formed from lieu.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: instead of（代替）最普通、最中性；in place of（代替）强调占据原有位置或履行原有作用；as a substitute for（作为……的替代品）明确强调替代关系。in lieu of 更正式，常见于雇佣、支付和补偿语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Instead of is the ordinary neutral equivalent; in place of emphasizes taking another item's position or role; as a substitute for makes the replacement relationship explicit. In lieu of is more formal and often occurs in employment, payment, and compensation contexts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lieu 的历史核心是“位置”：放到对方的位置上，就是“代替”。整块记忆 in lieu of。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The historical core of lieu is place: taking another thing's place means replacing it. Learn in lieu of as one unit.

meaning: 小姐；传统上用于称呼未婚法国女子

pronunciation.note: 采用 Collins 所列英式读音；末音节重读。

forms: 复数 mesdemoiselles，也有 mademoiselles；作姓氏前的称谓时写 Mademoiselle。
family: demoiselle 少女；madame 夫人

morphology.text: ma（法语：我的）+ demoiselle（少女）→ mademoiselle（小姐）；这是法语结构，英语中整体借用。

etymology.text: 由古法语 ma damoisele“我的年轻女士”经中古法语进入中古英语，后来沿用为称谓。把它与传统的法语礼貌称呼联系起来。

usage_note: 作为称谓相当于 Miss，传统上区别于 Madame；姓氏前通常大写。现代称呼应尊重对方偏好，不由自己推断婚姻身份。 本卡用作称谓，展示拼写为 Mademoiselle。

senses.meaning_zh: 小姐；传统上用于称呼或指称未婚法国女子的法语称谓
senses.meaning_en: A French title traditionally used for an unmarried woman, or a woman addressed by that title.
senses.english_definition: Mademoiselle is a French title traditionally used before the name of an unmarried woman or when speaking politely to her.
senses.collocation_en: Mademoiselle Dupont; Bonjour, Mademoiselle
senses.collocation_zh: 杜邦小姐；您好，小姐
senses.sentence_en: In the novel, Mademoiselle Dupont teaches music at a small village school.
senses.sentence_zh: 在这部小说中，杜邦小姐在一所乡村小学校教授音乐。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借用了法语 mademoiselle，由 ma“我的”和 demoiselle“年轻女士”组成，原是表示礼貌或尊敬的称呼。demoiselle 可追溯到拉丁语 domina“女主人”的指小形式；这一称谓后来传统上用于未婚女子。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French mademoiselle, formed from ma meaning my and demoiselle meaning young lady, originally a respectful form of address. Demoiselle ultimately derives from a diminutive of Latin domina, meaning mistress or lady, and the title became traditionally associated with unmarried women.

morphology_enriched.zh: 法语内部结构为 ma（我的，阴性形式）＋demoiselle（年轻女士）；英语将其作为整体借入，并没有现代英语前后缀可拆。传统复数为 mesdemoiselles；称谓缩写为 Mlle，复数缩写为 Mlles。demoiselle 和同源的 damsel（少女）是相关词，不是从英语 mademoiselle 派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: Its internal French structure is ma, the feminine form of my, plus demoiselle meaning young lady; English borrows the whole expression without adding English affixes. The traditional plural is mesdemoiselles; the title is abbreviated Mlle, with plural Mlles. Demoiselle and its relative damsel are related words rather than derivatives of English mademoiselle.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Miss（小姐）是传统上最接近的英语称谓；Ms（女士）不表明婚姻状况；Madame（女士；夫人）是另一个法语称谓，传统上与已婚女子相关，也用于礼貌称呼成年女子。Mademoiselle 带有明确的法语文化色彩，其传统用法暗含未婚身份。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Miss is the closest traditional English title; Ms does not indicate marital status; Madame is another French title, traditionally associated with married women and also used as a polite address for adult women. Mademoiselle carries a specifically French cultural association and traditionally implies unmarried status.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ma＝我的，demoiselle＝年轻女士：字面上的“我的年轻女士”，形成传统称谓“小姐”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ma means my and demoiselle means young lady: my young lady became the traditional title Mademoiselle.

meaning: 第纳尔；若干国家的货币单位

etymology.text: 英语借自阿拉伯语 dīnār，后者经晚期希腊语 denarion 上溯拉丁语 denarius，一种古罗马钱币名称。记住沿着贸易传播的货币名。

usage_note: dinar 是货币单位名称；必须看国家或货币代码，不能把不同国家的第纳尔当成同一种钱。

senses.meaning_zh: 第纳尔；若干国家的货币单位
senses.meaning_en: a monetary unit used in several countries
senses.english_definition: A dinar is a unit of money used in several countries, including Iraq, Jordan, and Kuwait.
senses.collocation_en: the Iraqi dinar; dinar-denominated bonds
senses.collocation_zh: 伊拉克第纳尔；以第纳尔计价的债券

etymology_story.zh: 英语 dinar 借自阿拉伯语 dīnār，最终源自拉丁语 dēnārius，即古罗马的一种钱币。这个名称随着货币制度和贸易传播，被多个地区沿用为货币名称。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed dinar from Arabic dīnār, ultimately from Latin dēnārius, the name of a Roman coin. The name spread through monetary systems and trade and became a currency name in several regions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，dinar 是不可进一步分析的借入词，不宜强拆为英语词根和词缀。复数为 dinars；常见复合形式有 dinar-denominated（以第纳尔计价的）和 dinar-based（以第纳尔为基础的），没有常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dinar is an unanalyzed loanword, with no productive English root-and-affix breakdown. Its plural is dinars; compounds include dinar-denominated and dinar-based, but there are no common direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有精确近义词。currency（货币）泛指一国或地区使用的货币；monetary unit（货币单位）是上位概念；denomination（面额）指货币的具体价值等级，不能直接替换 dinar。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym. Currency refers broadly to a monetary system or its money; monetary unit is the broader category; denomination identifies a particular face value and cannot directly replace dinar.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一枚罗马钱币的名字，沿着贸易路线变成多国货币名：dinar＝第纳尔。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A Roman coin name travels along trade routes and becomes the name of several currencies: dinar.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音符号标出重读音节。

etymology.text: 中古英语从盎格鲁法语 retenue 借入，与 retenir“留住、保留”有关。可以联想被重要人物留在身边的一群助手。

etymology_story.zh: retinue 经盎格鲁法语 retenue 进入中古英语，与意为“留住、雇用”的 retenir 有关。它原指被留用、为某人效劳的一群人，后来主要指重要人物身边的随从团。
etymology_story.en: Retinue entered Middle English through Anglo-French retenue, associated with retenir, meaning 'to retain or employ.' It referred to people retained in someone's service and developed the sense of an important person's accompanying attendants.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，retinue 作为完整词干使用，不应拆成 re- 加虚构词根；复数为 retinues，没有常用的直接派生词。同源相关词包括 retain（保留、雇用）、retainer（受雇随从；聘用费）、retention（保留）和 retentive（记性好的；有保持能力的），它们并非由 retinue 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats retinue as a whole stem, not as re- plus a separate English root; its plural is retinues, and it has no common direct derivatives. Related words include retain, retainer, retention, and retentive, but these are historical relatives rather than derivatives of retinue.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: entourage（随行团）常用于名人或公众人物，现代感较强；attendants（随从、侍从）强调服务职责；escort（护送人员）强调陪同和保护。retinue 较正式，常带宫廷或等级色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Entourage commonly describes the people around a celebrity or public figure; attendants emphasizes service; escort emphasizes accompaniment and protection. Retinue is more formal and often suggests a court or social hierarchy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 retain 的“留在身边”连到人群：被重要人物留在身边服务的人，就是 retinue。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with retain: people retained at an important person's side form a retinue.

usage_note: governess 常见于历史或文学语境，工作重点是家庭教育；nanny 主要照料孩子的日常生活。

etymology_story.zh: governess 源于中古英语 governeress 的缩略形式，后者来自古法语 gouverneresse，原指女性管理者。这个词后来专门用于负责私人家庭中儿童教育的女性。
etymology_story.en: Governess developed as a shortened form of Middle English governeress, from Old French gouverneresse, originally meaning a female governor or administrator. Its meaning later narrowed to a woman responsible for educating children in a private household.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可理解为 govern（管理、指导）＋-ess（传统女性称谓后缀），但实际词形经历了历史缩略；复数为 governesses。相关词族包括 govern（管理）、governor（管理者；总督）、governorship（总督等的职位）、government（政府；治理）、governmental（政府的）、governance（治理）、governing（管理的）、governable（可治理的）和 ungovernable（难以管束的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be understood through govern plus the traditional feminine suffix -ess, although its actual form reflects historical shortening; the plural is governesses. The related family includes govern, governor, governorship, government, governmental, governance, governing, governable, and ungovernable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: private tutor（私人教师）不限性别，也不一定在雇主家中长期任职；home tutor（家庭教师）强调在家授课；nanny（保姆）主要负责日常照料。governess 特指女性，核心职责是家庭教育。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A private tutor may be of any gender and need not hold a continuing household position; a home tutor emphasizes teaching at home; a nanny mainly provides everyday care. A governess is specifically a woman whose central responsibility is household education.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: govern 的“指导”＋女性后缀 -ess：在家中指导孩子学习的女性。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Govern suggests guiding, and -ess marks a woman: a woman who guides children's learning at home.

senses.collocation_en: the zeta function; zeta potential
senses.collocation_zh: 泽塔函数；ζ 电位
senses.sentence_en: The lowercase Greek letter zeta is written ζ.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 zeta 源自希腊语字母名 zēta，经拉丁语传入；该字母历史上承接了腓尼基字母 zayin。它一直保留字母名称的功能，后来广泛用于数学和科学符号。
etymology_story.en: English zeta comes through Latin from the Greek letter name zēta; the letter historically descends from Phoenician zayin. It retained its role as a letter name and later became widely used in mathematical and scientific notation.

morphology_enriched.zh: zeta 是完整的借入字母名，不能拆为现代英语词根和词缀；复数为 zetas。常见术语组合有 zeta function（泽塔函数）、zeta potential（ζ 电位）和 zeta distribution（泽塔分布）；这些是术语组合，不是独立词性的证据，也不是后缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Zeta is a complete borrowed letter name, with no modern English root-and-affix breakdown; its plural is zetas. Technical combinations include zeta function, zeta potential, and zeta distribution; these are compound terms rather than suffix derivatives or evidence of a separate part of speech.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有普通词汇意义上的近义词。Ζ 和 ζ 分别是其大写、小写符号；the sixth Greek letter（第六个希腊字母）是解释性同指表达；Greek letter（希腊字母）只是上位概念。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There are no ordinary lexical synonyms. Ζ and ζ are its uppercase and lowercase symbols; the sixth Greek letter is an explanatory equivalent; Greek letter is only the broader category.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一名两形、位置第六：zeta＝Ζ／ζ。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One name, two shapes, sixth position: zeta = Ζ/ζ.

senses.meaning_zh: 对数；给定底数得到某个正数时所需的指数
senses.meaning_en: the exponent to which a given base must be raised to produce a number
senses.english_definition: The logarithm of a positive number to a particular base is the power to which you must raise that base to obtain the number.

etymology_story.zh: 约翰·纳皮尔在其 1614 年的著作中使用新拉丁语 logarithmus，以希腊语 logos（比例、关系）和 arithmos（数）构成这个名称。对数把乘法关系转化为加法关系，因而曾是简化复杂计算的重要工具。
etymology_story.en: John Napier used the New Latin term logarithmus in his 1614 publication, forming it from Greek logos, meaning 'ratio or relation,' and arithmos, meaning 'number.' Logarithms turn multiplicative relationships into additive ones and became an important tool for simplifying calculations.

morphology_enriched.zh: logarithm 在现代英语中通常作为完整数学词干使用，历史构件为 log-（比例）＋arithm-（数），不可把开头误解为普通英语 log（木头）。词族包括 logarithms（复数）、logarithmic（对数的）、logarithmically（按对数关系地）、log（缩略形式）、antilogarithm／antilog（反对数）、antilogarithmic（反对数的）及 semilogarithmic（半对数的）；相关复合词包括 log-normal／lognormal（对数正态的）和 log-linear／loglinear（对数线性的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats logarithm as a complete mathematical stem; its historical elements are log- 'ratio' and arithm- 'number,' unrelated to ordinary English log meaning a piece of wood. Its family includes logarithms, logarithmic, logarithmically, the shortening log, antilogarithm or antilog, antilogarithmic, and semilogarithmic; related compounds include log-normal or lognormal and log-linear or loglinear.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: log（对数）是 logarithm 的常用缩略形式；natural logarithm（自然对数）专指以 e 为底的对数；common logarithm（常用对数）专指以 10 为底的对数。后两者是下位类型，不能在底数不明确时任意替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Log is the usual shortened equivalent of logarithm; natural logarithm specifically uses base e; common logarithm specifically uses base 10. The latter two are particular types and are interchangeable with logarithm only when the base is appropriate.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 对数就是“问指数”：10 的几次方是 100？答案 2，就是相应的对数。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A logarithm asks for the exponent: what power of 10 gives 100? The answer, 2, is the logarithm.

etymology.text: 至少在16世纪的早期现代英语中就已使用 shrivel，并沿用至今，描写失水后缩小起皱的样子。联想葡萄慢慢变成葡萄干的外观。

usage_note: shrivel 常同时强调干燥、变小和起皱；shrink 只强调变小，未必干枯。

senses.meaning_zh: 因失水而干枯皱缩；使干枯皱缩
senses.meaning_en: to become, or make something, dry, smaller, and wrinkled
senses.english_definition: If something shrivels, or something shrivels it, it becomes smaller and wrinkled, usually because it loses moisture.
senses.collocation_en: shrivel up; shrivel in the heat
senses.collocation_zh: 干瘪皱缩；在高温下干枯皱缩
senses.sentence_en: The grapes began to shrivel in the hot sun.
senses.sentence_zh: 葡萄在烈日下开始干瘪皱缩。

senses.english_definition: If confidence, hope, or another quality shrivels, it becomes much weaker; if you shrivel inside, you feel painfully embarrassed or afraid.

senses.sentence_zh: 意识到所有人都听出了她的错误时，她窘迫得恨不得缩成一团。

etymology_story.zh: shrivel 至少从16世纪起见于英语，其更早的来源尚不确定。它由描写物体干枯皱缩，进一步发展出力量、信心等衰退以及人因难堪而畏缩的比喻义。
etymology_story.en: Shrivel has been recorded in English since at least the sixteenth century, although its earlier origin is uncertain. Its physical meaning of drying and wrinkling developed figurative uses for declining strength or confidence and emotional withdrawal.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，shrivel 是不能可靠拆分为常用词根和词缀的动词词基。常用变化：shrivels；shrivelling、shrivelled（英式）；shriveling、shriveled（美式）；过去分词也可作形容词，表示“干瘪的”。常见短语为 shrivel up；不宜把词尾误拆为具有独立意义的 -el。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, shrivel is a verb base without a useful division into familiar roots and affixes. Its common forms are shrivels, British shrivelling and shrivelled, and American shriveling and shriveled; the past participle also functions adjectivally, meaning dry and wrinkled. A common phrasal form is shrivel up; the ending -el should not be assigned a separate meaning.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: shrink（缩小）只强调尺寸减小；wither（枯萎）强调植物失去水分和生机；wrinkle（起皱）强调表面出现皱纹。shrivel 通常兼有干燥、缩小和起皱三层意思。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Shrink emphasizes reduced size, wither emphasizes the loss of moisture and vitality in plants, and wrinkle emphasizes folds in a surface. Shrivel typically combines drying, shrinking, and wrinkling.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象葡萄失水变成葡萄干：水少了，体积缩了，表皮皱了；信心也可以这样“萎缩”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a grape becoming a raisin: moisture disappears, size decreases, and wrinkles appear; confidence can metaphorically shrivel in the same way.

usage_note: afresh 常表示带着新起点或新方法再做一次；again 可以只是普通重复。

senses.meaning_zh: 重新；从头再来；以新的方式
senses.meaning_en: again, especially from a new beginning or in a new way
senses.english_definition: If you do something afresh, you do it again, often by making a new beginning or taking a new approach.
senses.collocation_en: start afresh; look at something afresh
senses.collocation_zh: 重新开始；以新的眼光审视某事
senses.sentence_en: After the first plan failed, we decided to start afresh.
senses.sentence_zh: 第一个计划失败后，我们决定从头再来。

etymology_story.zh: afresh 源于中古英语，由副词性成分 a- 与 fresh（新的、新鲜的）组合而成。其意义由“以新鲜的状态或方式”发展为“重新、从头开始”。
etymology_story.en: Afresh developed in Middle English from the adverb-forming element a- and fresh. The idea of doing something freshly or in a new way developed into the meaning of beginning or doing it again.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：a-（构成副词的历史成分）+ fresh（新的）→ afresh；它是固定副词，没有比较级或常用直接派生词。fresh 的常用相关词族包括 freshly（新近地；新鲜地）、freshness（新鲜）、freshen（使变清新）、refresh（使恢复精神；刷新）、refreshed（恢复精神的）、refreshing（令人精神振奋的）、refresher（复习课程等）和 refreshment（恢复精力；茶点）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: a- (a historical adverb-forming element) + fresh → afresh. It is a fixed adverb with no comparative form or common direct derivatives. The related fresh family includes freshly, freshness, freshen, refresh, refreshed, refreshing, refresher, and refreshment.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: anew（重新）与 afresh 接近，但更偏书面；again（再次）只表示重复，不一定有新起点；from scratch（从零开始）更明确地表示不依靠现成成果。afresh 强调重新出发或换一种眼光。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Anew is close in meaning but more literary; again indicates repetition without necessarily suggesting a new beginning; from scratch more explicitly means starting without an existing foundation. Afresh emphasizes a fresh start or perspective.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: a- + fresh：给事情一个“新的开始”，就是 afresh。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect afresh with fresh: give the task a fresh beginning.

etymology.text: 英语音乐用语 techno 来自 techno-pop、techno-rock 等名称中的 techno-，该形式与 technology 相连，突出了电子设备制作声音的特点。

senses.meaning_zh: 特克诺电子舞曲；以持续规则节拍和电子音色为特征的舞曲类型
senses.meaning_en: a style of electronic dance music characterized by a steady, repetitive beat
senses.english_definition: Techno is a type of electronic dance music that uses a strong, regular beat and repeated electronic sounds.
senses.collocation_en: techno music; a techno track
senses.collocation_zh: 特克诺电子舞曲；一首特克诺舞曲
senses.sentence_en: The DJ played techno until the club closed.
senses.sentence_zh: DJ 一直播放特克诺舞曲，直到俱乐部打烊。

etymology_story.zh: 音乐名称 techno 与表示技术的构词成分 techno- 有关，后者最终可追溯到希腊语 tekhnē，意为“技艺”。这一名称在20世纪80年代逐渐与底特律发展起来的一种电子舞曲风格紧密相连。
etymology_story.en: The musical name techno is connected with techno-, the combining form referring to technology, ultimately from Greek tekhnē, meaning art or craft. During the 1980s, the name became closely associated with an electronic dance style developed in Detroit.

morphology_enriched.zh: 作为音乐名称，techno 是独立的不可数名词；在 techno music、techno producer 中通常是名词作前置修饰语，不必另列为普通形容词。须区分音乐名词 techno 与构词成分 techno-：后者见于 technopop（电子流行乐）、technophobia（技术恐惧）和 technophile（技术爱好者）；technology（技术）、technological（技术的）、technologically（在技术上）属于相关技术词族，并非都由音乐名词派生。
morphology_enriched.en: As a musical name, techno is an independent uncountable noun. In techno music and techno producer, it normally functions as a noun modifier rather than requiring a separate ordinary adjective entry. Distinguish the musical noun from the combining form techno-, found in technopop, technophobia, and technophile; technology, technological, and technologically belong to the related technology family, rather than deriving from the musical noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全等义的常用替换词。electronic dance music／EDM（电子舞曲）是包含 techno 的上位概念；house（浩室舞曲）是相邻但不同的舞曲类型；electronica（电子音乐）范围较宽，也可包含不以舞蹈为目的的音乐。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact common synonym. Electronic dance music, or EDM, is a broader category that includes techno; house is a related but distinct dance genre; electronica is a broader term that can also include music not primarily intended for dancing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: techno 联系 technology：用电子技术制造持续、规则的舞池节拍。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link techno with technology: electronically generated sounds arranged around a steady dance-floor beat.

usage_note: principality 指与王公头衔或统治权相关的领地；republic 指共和国，政治体制不同。

senses.meaning_zh: 公国；亲王或王公统治的国家或领地

senses.english_definition: A principality is a country or territory whose ruler is a prince or princess.
senses.collocation_en: an independent principality; the Principality of Monaco
senses.collocation_zh: 独立公国；摩纳哥公国
senses.sentence_en: The treaty recognized the territory as an independent principality.
senses.sentence_zh: 该条约承认这片领土为独立公国。

etymology_story.zh: principality 经法语进入中古英语，最终源于拉丁语 principalitas，原指首要地位或最高权力，与 princeps（首领、居首者）有关。其意义后来具体化为王公的统治权及其统治的领地。
etymology_story.en: Principality entered Middle English through French and ultimately comes from Latin principalitas, referring to pre-eminence or supreme authority, related to princeps, a leader or foremost person. Its meaning developed into princely rule and the territory governed under it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 形式上可分析为 principal + -ity，但这里承接的是“最高统治权、王公地位”的历史意义，不能按现代 principal 的“校长”义理解为“校长的领地”。本词常用变化为复数 principalities；相关词族包括 prince（王子；亲王）、princess（公主；女亲王；王妃）、princely（王公的；豪华的）、princeliness（王公气派）和 princeling（小王公；年轻王子）。
morphology_enriched.en: Its form can be analyzed as principal + -ity, but it preserves the historical sense of supreme or princely authority; it does not mean the territory of a modern school principal. Its regular plural is principalities. Related family members include prince, princess, princely, princeliness, and princeling.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: state（国家）不限定统治者头衔；duchy（公爵领地；公国）通常由公爵或女公爵统治；kingdom（王国）由国王或女王统治。principality 专指以亲王或相应王公为统治者的政治实体，不能与另外两种君主领地随意互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: State does not specify a ruler's title; duchy normally denotes a territory ruled by a duke or duchess; kingdom denotes one ruled by a king or queen. Principality specifically identifies a political entity under a prince or princess, so these monarchy terms are not freely interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 prince（亲王）的历史关联：亲王统治的领地，就是 principality。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use its historical connection with prince: a prince's territory is a principality.

meaning: 酸化的；经过加酸处理的

pronunciation.note: 由词典所列 acidify 的英式读音加过去分词词尾 /d/；-fy 的双元音保留。

forms: 对应动词 acidify；第三人称单数 acidifies；过去式及过去分词 acidified；现在分词 acidifying。
family: acid 酸；acidification 酸化

morphology.text: acid（酸）+ -ify（使成为）→ acidify（使酸化）；acidify + -ed → acidified（酸化的），变 y 为 i 再加 -ed。

etymology.text: acidify 借自法语 acidifier，由 acide 和 -ifier 组成；英语再用 -ed 形成 acidified。把它理解为已经过酸化处理的状态。

usage_note: acidified 强调发生过酸化过程；acidic 主要描述呈酸性的性质，不一定说明处理过程。

senses.pos: v. 动词（acidify 的过去式和过去分词）
senses.meaning_zh: 使酸化；使酸度增加；变得更酸
senses.meaning_en: made something more acidic, or became more acidic
senses.english_definition: If something acidified a substance, it made that substance more acidic; if the substance acidified, its acidity increased.
senses.collocation_en: acidified the solution; acidified with hydrochloric acid

senses.sentence_zh: 技术员加入几滴盐酸，使溶液酸化。

etymology_story.zh: acidified 是 acidify 的过去式和过去分词；acidify 中的 acid 最终源于拉丁语 acidus，意为“酸的”。使役后缀 -ify 最终与拉丁语 facere（使成为、制作）有关，因此全词表达“使变酸”这一过程完成后或过去发生的状态与动作。
etymology_story.en: Acidified is the past tense and past participle of acidify, whose element acid ultimately comes from Latin acidus, meaning sour. The causative suffix -ify ultimately relates to Latin facere, meaning to make, giving the verb the sense of making something more acidic.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：acid（酸；酸的）+ -ify（使成为）→ acidify（使酸化）；acidify 将词尾 y 改为 i，再加 -ed → acidified。常用词形及词族包括 acidifies、acidifying、acidified、acidification（酸化）、acidifier（酸化剂）、acidic（酸性的）、acidity（酸度）和 unacidified（未经酸化的）；其中 acidic、acidity 由 acid 词基形成。acidified 可作动词形式，也可作描述结果状态的分词形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: acid + -ify (make or cause to become) → acidify; change the final y to i and add -ed → acidified. Common forms and family members include acidifies, acidifying, acidified, acidification, acidifier, acidic, acidity, and unacidified; acidic and acidity are formed from the base acid. Acidified functions both as a verb form and as a participial adjective describing a resulting state.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: acidulated（加酸的；略带酸味的）常指食物或液体加入少量酸；acid-treated（经酸处理的）强调处理方法，目的未必只是提高酸度；acidic（酸性的）描述性质，不表示经历过酸化过程。acidified 强调酸度增加的过程或结果，并不必然表示最终 pH 已低于7。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Acidulated often describes food or liquid to which a small amount of acid has been added; acid-treated emphasizes a treatment method that may serve purposes beyond increasing acidity; acidic describes a property without implying a prior acidification process. Acidified emphasizes an increase in acidity or its result and does not necessarily mean that the final pH is below 7.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: acid + -ify + -ed：酸 → 使变酸 → 已经酸化；记住“发生过变化”，而不只是“具有酸性”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Acid + -ify + -ed: acid → make more acidic → already acidified. Remember the change or treatment behind the resulting state.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音符号标出重读音节。

forms: 形容词，没有复数或时态变化。
family: endogenously 内生地；endogenicity 内生性

morphology.text: endo-（内部）+ -genous（产生的）→ endogenous（内生的）。

etymology.text: 19世纪英语科学用语，由 endo- 与 -genous 构成，两个部分取材于希腊语中“内部”和“产生”的概念。记住来源在系统自身内部。

usage_note: endogenous 来自系统或身体内部；exogenous 来自外部。必须先明确讨论的是哪个系统。

etymology_story.zh: endogenous 是19世纪形成的科学用语，由表示“内部”的 endo- 和表示“产生、起源”的 -genous 构成，两部分均源于希腊语。其“从内部产生”的含义后来也用于经济学等领域，描述系统内部形成的结果。
etymology_story.en: Endogenous developed as a scientific term in the nineteenth century from endo-, meaning 'within,' and -genous, referring to production or origin, both of Greek origin. Its meaning of arising from within was later applied in fields such as economics to outcomes generated inside a system.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：endo-（内部）+ -genous（产生的、起源于……的）。主要词族：endogenously（内生地、内源性地）、endogeneity（内生性）、endogeny（内生、内源发生）；经济学中还有 endogenize（使内生化）和 endogenization（内生化），英式拼写也用 endogenise、endogenisation。相关构词 endogenesis 指“内源发生”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: endo- 'within' + -genous 'produced in or originating from.' Principal family members include endogenously, endogeneity, and endogeny; economics also uses endogenize and endogenization, with British variants endogenise and endogenisation. The related formation endogenesis means development or production from within.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: internal（内部的）只说明位置或关系，不一定说明来源；intrinsic（内在的、固有的）强调事物本身具有的性质；homegrown（本土产生的、自行发展的）较通俗，常用于组织或地区。endogenous 专门强调产生原因或来源在系统内部。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Internal describes location or relationship without necessarily identifying origin; intrinsic describes a quality inherent in something; homegrown is less technical and often refers to development within an organization or region. Endogenous specifically identifies a source or cause within the system.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: endo-＝里面，-genous＝产生：原因或产物来自“自己内部”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Endo- means 'inside' and -genous points to production: the source is inside the system itself.

senses.meaning_zh: 管腔；血管、肠道等管状结构的内部空间

etymology_story.zh: lumen 借自拉丁语 lūmen，意为“光”，也可指让光线通过的开口。英语中的流明单位义承接“光”的含义，解剖学中的管腔义则承接“开口、内部通道”的含义。
etymology_story.en: Lumen comes from Latin lūmen, meaning 'light' and also an opening through which light enters. Its measurement sense preserves the connection with light, while its anatomical sense develops the idea of an opening or internal passage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 lumen 通常作为不可再分析的借词词干。单位义的复数是 lumens；解剖学义常用拉丁式复数 lumina，也可用 lumens。解剖学词族使用 lumin-：luminal（管腔的）、intraluminal（管腔内的）、extraluminal（管腔外的）、transluminal（经管腔的）。计量复合词有 lumen-hour（流明小时）；luminous（发光的）与 illuminate（照亮）是同源词，并非现代英语中直接由 lumen 加后缀构成。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, lumen is generally treated as an unanalyzed borrowed stem. The measurement plural is lumens; the anatomical plural is commonly lumina, although lumens also occurs. Anatomical derivatives use lumin-: luminal, intraluminal, extraluminal, and transluminal. A measurement compound is lumen-hour; luminous and illuminate are historical relatives rather than direct modern suffixations of lumen.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cavity（腔、空腔）泛指内部空隙；channel（通道）强调供物质通过的路径；bore（孔径、内孔）多用于管道或机械零件。lumen 特指管状结构内部的空间；作为光通量单位时没有可直接替换的近义词，lux（勒克斯）衡量的是单位面积接收到的光通量。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cavity is a general internal hollow; channel emphasizes a passage through which something travels; bore commonly refers to the internal hole or diameter of a tube or mechanical part. Lumen specifically names a tubular structure's inner space. Its unit sense has no interchangeable synonym: lux measures luminous flux received per unit area.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拉丁语“光”连接流明，“透光的开口”连接管腔：一个词抓住“光”和“通道”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect Latin 'light' with the lighting unit, and a light-admitting opening with a hollow passage.

etymology_story.zh: mutton 经中古英语进入英语，源自盎格鲁法语 mutun，原来既可指绵羊，也可指羊肉。在英语中，它逐渐主要指成年绵羊的肉，而表示动物本身的日常词仍是 sheep。
etymology_story.en: Mutton entered Middle English from Anglo-French mutun, which could refer both to a sheep and to its meat. In English, it became primarily the name for meat from an adult sheep, while sheep remained the everyday word for the animal.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：mutton 是不可再分析的单纯词，表示肉时通常不可数。常见复合词有 mutton chop（成年绵羊排）和 muttonchops（形似羊排的浓密鬓须）；较少见的派生词 muttony 表示“有羊肉味的”。muttonhead（笨蛋）和 muttonheaded（愚笨的）是带贬义的非正式构词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: mutton is a simple, unanalyzed word and is normally uncountable when referring to meat. Common compounds include mutton chop and muttonchops, the latter also naming thick sideburns shaped like chops. The uncommon derivative muttony means tasting or smelling of mutton; muttonhead and muttonheaded are informal, disparaging formations meaning a fool and foolish.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lamb（羔羊肉）来自幼羊，通常更嫩；hogget（青年羊肉）是英国等地用于介于羔羊与成年羊之间的羊肉名称；goat meat（山羊肉）来自动物山羊，在标准英美英语中不等于 mutton，但在南亚英语中常被称为 mutton。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lamb comes from young sheep and is generally more tender; hogget is a regional term, used in Britain and elsewhere, for meat from sheep between the lamb and mature stages; goat meat comes from goats and is distinct from mutton in standard British and American usage, although South Asian English often calls it mutton.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sheep 在牧场，mutton 上餐桌；lamb 偏幼羊，mutton 指成年羊肉。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sheep names the animal; mutton names its meat. Contrast young lamb with mature mutton.

etymology_story.zh: superstructure 在17世纪由 super-（在……之上）与 structure（结构）组合而成，最初表示建在某个基础之上的实体结构。这一空间关系后来被用于抽象体系，并在马克思主义理论中获得“经济基础之上的制度和观念体系”这一专门含义。
etymology_story.en: Superstructure was formed in the seventeenth century from super-, meaning 'above,' and structure, initially for a physical structure built on a base. This spatial relationship later extended to abstract systems and acquired a specialized meaning in Marxist accounts of institutions and ideas resting on an economic base.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：super-（在……上面）+ structure（结构）。直接词族：superstructures（复数）、superstructural（上部结构的；上层建筑的）、superstructurally（从上部结构或上层建筑方面）。基础词族包括 structure、structural（结构的）、structurally（在结构上）；substructure（下部结构）与 infrastructure（基础设施）是使用同一基础词的相关构词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: super- 'above' + structure. Direct family members include the plural superstructures, the adjective superstructural, and the adverb superstructurally. The base family includes structure, structural, and structurally; substructure and infrastructure are related formations built on the same base.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: upper structure（上部结构）是直白的空间描述；framework（框架）强调支撑或组织整体的骨架，不限定在上方；edifice（大厦；庞大体系）强调建筑或思想体系的整体规模。superstructure 特别强调其与下方基础的依托关系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Upper structure is a plain spatial description; framework emphasizes the supporting or organizing skeleton without specifying an upper position; edifice emphasizes an imposing building or elaborate intellectual system. Superstructure specifically highlights dependence on an underlying base.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: super-＝在上，structure＝结构：实体在地基之上，制度和观念在经济基础之上。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Super- means 'above': picture a structure above its foundation, then ideas and institutions above an economic base.

senses.collocation_en: bumble around the room; bumble into a room
senses.collocation_zh: 在房间里笨拙地转来转去；跌跌撞撞地走进房间
senses.sentence_en: Still half asleep, he bumbled around the room looking for his glasses.
senses.sentence_zh: 他仍然半睡半醒，笨拙地在房间里转来转去找眼镜。

etymology_story.zh: 表示笨拙行事的 bumble 在16世纪已有记录，通常被认为与 bungle（把事情搞砸）有关，但具体形成过程并不确定。英语中还曾有表示“嗡嗡响”的 bumble，这一声音义保留在 bumblebee（熊蜂）中，不宜把“笨拙”的含义直接当作该复合词的历史来源。
etymology_story.en: Bumble in the sense of acting clumsily is recorded in the sixteenth century and is generally connected with bungle, although its precise formation is uncertain. English also had a bumble meaning 'to buzz,' preserved in bumblebee, whose historical formation should not simply be explained through clumsiness.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bumble 通常作为单纯动词整体分析。屈折形式：bumbles、bumbled、bumbling，添加 -ing 时去掉词尾不发音的 e。派生词：bumbler（做事笨拙的人，bumble 去 e 加 -er）、bumbling（笨拙无能的，也可作形容词）、bumblingly（笨拙地，较少见）。bumblebee 是与历史上的“嗡嗡响”义相关的复合词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: bumble is normally analyzed as a simple verb. Its inflected forms are bumbles, bumbled, and bumbling; the silent final e is dropped before -ing. Derivatives include bumbler, formed by dropping e and adding -er; the adjective bumbling; and the uncommon adverb bumblingly. Bumblebee is a compound associated with the historical buzzing sense.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bungle（搞砸）强调把任务处理得很差；blunder（犯大错；莽撞地移动）强调明显错误或粗心行动；fumble（笨手笨脚地摸索；结结巴巴地应付）常强调手部动作或临场表达不顺。bumble 更突出一连串笨拙、迷糊而缺乏效率的行为。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bungle emphasizes handling a task badly; blunder emphasizes a conspicuous mistake or careless movement; fumble often concerns awkward hand movements or hesitant performance under pressure. Bumble suggests an ongoing pattern of clumsy, confused, ineffective behavior.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 bumble 联想为“边绊边忙”：走路磕绊，办事也磕绊；这是记忆联想，并非词源解释。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture someone stumbling while trying to get things done: awkward movement becomes awkward action. This is a memory association, not an etymology.

family: vaned 有叶片的；weather vane 风向标

morphology.text: vane 作为独立词素整词记忆；vane + -ed → vaned（有叶片的，词尾只加 d）。

usage_note: 本课指显示风向的装置；在机械中还可指叶片。与 vain、vein 同音，拼写和意义不同。

etymology_story.zh: vane 经中古英语 vane、fane 源自古英语 fana，原意是“旗帜”。词义从迎风飘动的旗帜发展为指示风向的装置，后来也用于机器中引导气流或液流的叶片。
etymology_story.en: Vane comes through Middle English vane and fane from Old English fana, meaning “banner.” Its meaning developed from a flag exposed to the wind to a wind-direction indicator and later to blades that guide flowing air or liquid.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 vane 是不可再作常用词缀拆分的基本词：vane + -s → vanes（复数）；vane + -d → vaned（有叶片的）；vane 去掉词尾 e 加 -less → vaneless（无叶片的）。常见复合词有 weather + vane → weathervane（风向标），也写作 weather vane。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, vane is a base word with no useful division into smaller productive parts: vane + -s → vanes; vane + -d → vaned, meaning fitted with vanes; and vane with final e removed + -less → vaneless. A common compound is weather + vane → weathervane, also written weather vane.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: weathercock（鸡形风向标）强调传统的公鸡造型；windsock（风向袋）是显示风向并粗略反映风力的布筒；blade（叶片）适用于机械义，但范围更广，也可指旋转切割部件。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Weathercock specifically suggests a traditional rooster-shaped wind indicator; windsock is a fabric tube that indicates wind direction and roughly shows wind strength; blade overlaps with the mechanical sense but is broader and can also describe a rotating cutting part.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“迎风的旗”记到“指风的标”；机器里的 vane 则引导流体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a banner responding to the wind: a vane indicates wind direction or guides a flowing fluid.

usage_note: 常见木制或橡胶槌头，也用于槌球、马球及打击乐；并非所有 mallet 都由木头制成。

etymology_story.zh: mallet 经中古英语借自盎格鲁法语 maillet，是 mail（锤）的指小形式，可追溯至拉丁语 malleus（锤）。它后来用于多种带槌头的器具，包括工具、球槌和打击乐槌。
etymology_story.en: Mallet entered Middle English from Anglo-French maillet, a diminutive of mail, meaning “hammer,” ultimately from Latin malleus. It came to name several headed striking implements, including tools, sports equipment, and percussion sticks.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 mallet 通常作为完整基本词学习，不把历史上的指小成分当作现代后缀：mallet + -s → mallets（复数）。相关复合表达有 mallet-headed（槌头状的）、mallet percussion（槌击打击乐器类）和 mallet player（演奏槌击打击乐器的人）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats mallet as a whole base word; its historical diminutive ending is not a productive suffix here. Mallet + -s → mallets. Related compounds and expressions include mallet-headed, meaning having a mallet-shaped head; mallet percussion, referring to percussion instruments played with mallets; and mallet player.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hammer（锤）是更广泛的敲击工具名称，常有金属头；beater（敲击棒、打击棒）强调敲击功能，在音乐语境中可与 mallet 部分重合；club（棍棒、球杆）强调棒状器具，不一定具有明显的槌头。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hammer is a broader name for a striking tool and often suggests a metal head; beater emphasizes the striking function and can overlap with mallet in musical contexts; club emphasizes a stick-like implement and does not necessarily have a distinct mallet head.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“柄端有槌头”：敲木料、击球、奏乐都能用 mallet。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember a handle with a striking head: a mallet can tap wood, hit a ball, or play music.

pronunciation.note: 重音在第一音节；这里采用常见美式 /ɑː/ 读音。

etymology.text: 19世纪英语中的 toffee 是 taffy 的变体，后来常指糖与黄油煮成、冷却后变硬的糖果。联想那种香甜黏牙的口感。

senses.meaning_en: a hard or chewy sweet made by cooking sugar and butter
senses.english_definition: Toffee is a hard or chewy sweet made by heating sugar and butter together, and a toffee is an individual piece of this sweet.

etymology_story.zh: toffee 在19世纪初见于英语，与 taffy 有关，但更早的词源并不确定。后来，toffee 通常指糖与黄油熬成的糖果，而 taffy 在美式英语中通常指经过拉扯制成的耐嚼糖。
etymology_story.en: Toffee appeared in English in the early nineteenth century and is related to taffy, although its ultimate origin is uncertain. Toffee came to refer especially to sweets made from cooked sugar and butter, while American taffy usually refers to a chewy sweet made by pulling the cooked mixture.

morphology_enriched.zh: toffee 是现代基本词，没有可可靠拆分的常用词根和词缀。作物质名词时通常不可数，指单颗糖时可数，复数为 toffees；常见组合有 toffee apple（太妃糖衣苹果）和 toffee sauce（太妃糖酱）。toffee-nosed（势利的）虽然拼写含 toffee，但历史上与 toff（上流社会人物）有关，不能按糖果义直接推导。
morphology_enriched.en: Toffee is a modern base word without a reliable productive root-and-affix breakdown. It is usually uncountable as a substance but countable for individual sweets, with the plural toffees. Common combinations include toffee apple and toffee sauce. Although toffee-nosed means snobbish and contains the spelling toffee, it is historically associated with toff, an upper-class person, rather than being directly explained by the sweet.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: caramel（焦糖、卡拉蜜糖）与 toffee 的用法有重叠，但更强调糖加热后的焦糖化风味，也可指软糖或酱；fudge（法奇软糖）通常更软，质地细密；taffy（拉糖）强调通过拉扯形成的耐嚼质地。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Caramel overlaps with toffee but emphasizes the flavor of caramelized sugar and can also mean a soft sweet or sauce; fudge is usually softer with a fine-textured consistency; taffy emphasizes a chewy texture produced by pulling the mixture.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 糖加黄油熬浓，冷却成太妃糖。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sugar and butter cooked together, then cooled: picture toffee.

etymology_story.zh: typeface 由印刷意义的 type（活字、印刷字）和 face（表面、外观）组成，与活字上承印的字面有关。它后来用于表示一套字符共有的视觉设计，并沿用至数字排版。
etymology_story.en: Typeface combines type, in its printing sense, with face, referring to the visible or printing surface of a piece of type. It developed into a term for the shared visual design of a set of characters and continued into digital typography.

morphology_enriched.zh: type（印刷字）+ face（字面、外观）→ typeface；typeface + -s → typefaces（复数）。typeface 本身没有常用的直接派生动词或形容词；同一 type 构词网络中的相关词有 typeset（排版）、typesetter（排字工、排版人员）和 typesetting（排版），它们并非由 typeface 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Type, meaning printing characters, + face, meaning their visible form, → typeface; typeface + -s → typefaces. Typeface has no common directly derived verb or adjective. Related words built on type include typeset, typesetter, and typesetting, but these are not derivatives of typeface itself.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: font（字体、字库）在日常数字使用中常与 typeface 互换，严格区分时可指某种具体字重、样式的实现或字体文件；lettering（字体设计、字样）侧重绘制或安排字母的形式；type style（字体样式）是较宽泛的说法，也可能专指粗体、斜体等样式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Font is often interchangeable with typeface in everyday digital use, but in a stricter distinction it can refer to a specific weight or style implementation or a font file; lettering emphasizes drawn or arranged letterforms; type style is broader and can also refer specifically to styles such as bold or italic.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: type 是字，face 是面貌：typeface 就是文字的一套共同面貌。

etymology_story.zh: billiard 与表示台球运动的 billiards 同源，来自法语 billard，早期可指球杆；更早的 bille 意为“木棍、木料”。英语中的 billiard 主要保留在 billiard table、billiard ball 等名词前的修饰用法中。
etymology_story.en: Billiard belongs with billiards and comes from French billard, which could originally refer to a playing stick, from bille, meaning a piece of wood or a stick. In English, billiard survives mainly before nouns in expressions such as billiard table and billiard ball.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 billiard 作为完整词基学习，不宜把 -ard 当作这里的现代能产后缀。相关形式 billiards 是运动名称，通常接单数谓语，并不是现代常用可数名词 billiard 的普通复数；常见组合有 billiard table（台球桌）、billiard ball（台球）和 billiard cue（台球杆）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, billiard is best learned as a whole base; -ard is not a productive modern suffix in this word. The related form billiards names the game and normally takes a singular verb; it is not the ordinary plural of a commonly used count noun billiard. Common combinations include billiard table, billiard ball, and billiard cue.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: billiards（台球运动）是对应的运动名词，地域不同，其范围可能不同；pool（普尔台球、落袋台球）通常指使用袋口的特定台球玩法；snooker（斯诺克）是具有独立规则的另一种台球运动，因此相关修饰语不能随意互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Billiards is the corresponding noun for the game, although its scope varies by region; pool usually refers to particular pocket-billiards games; snooker is another cue sport with its own rules, so their corresponding modifiers are not freely interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: billiards 是运动名称；放到 table、ball 前，常用 billiard。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Billiards names the game; before table or ball, remember billiard.

etymology_story.zh: canter 缩自 Canterbury gallop（坎特伯雷式跑马），传统上与前往英国坎特伯雷的骑马朝圣者所采用的舒缓步速有关。这个名称后来固定指介于快步与疾驰之间的三拍步态。
etymology_story.en: Canter is a shortening of Canterbury gallop, traditionally associated with the easy riding pace of pilgrims travelling to Canterbury in England. It came to denote the three-beat gait between a trot and a gallop.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 canter 是不可再作有效拆分的独立词基，兼作名词和动词。屈折形式：canters、cantered、cantering；派生词 canterer（以这种步态骑马的人）较少见；cantering 也可作分词形容词，表示“正在慢跑的”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, canter is a simplex base used as both a noun and a verb. Inflected forms are canters, cantered, and cantering; the derivative canterer, meaning someone who rides at a canter, is uncommon, and cantering can also function as a participial adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 相邻步态词：trot（快步）通常为两拍，速度一般较慢；gallop（疾驰）为四拍，通常更快；lope（轻快大步跑）强调轻松而有弹性的动作，也可指西部骑术中的慢跑步态。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related gait terms: trot usually describes a slower, two-beat gait; gallop describes a generally faster, four-beat gait; lope emphasizes easy, bounding movement and can denote the canter in Western riding.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象朝圣者骑马去 Canterbury：保持舒缓节奏前进，就是 canter。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture pilgrims riding comfortably to Canterbury: their easy pace anchors canter.

etymology.text: 英语借自新拉丁语，根源是希腊语 kirrhos（橙黄色）。这个名字让人想到病变肝脏的黄褐色外观。

etymology_story.zh: cirrhosis 是由希腊语 kirrhos（黄褐色、橙黄色）与表示病变状态的 -osis 构成的医学术语，经新拉丁语进入英语。名称最初着眼于某些病变肝脏的黄褐色外观，后来成为这种瘢痕性肝病的通称。
etymology_story.en: Cirrhosis is a medical formation from Greek kirrhos, meaning tawny or orange-yellow, and -osis, indicating a pathological condition, transmitted through New Latin. The name originally referred to the tawny appearance of some affected livers and became the established term for the scarring disease.

morphology_enriched.zh: 医学构词可分析为 cirrh-（源自“黄褐色”的历史词干）+ -osis（病变状态），但不能仅凭现代字面词根解释其病理含义。核心词族：cirrhosis（肝硬化）、cirrhotic（肝硬化的；名词用法指肝硬化患者）、noncirrhotic／non-cirrhotic（非肝硬化的）；复数为 cirrhoses。
morphology_enriched.en: The medical formation is cirrh-, a historical stem meaning tawny, plus -osis, meaning a pathological condition, although these elements alone do not explain the modern pathology. The core family includes cirrhosis, cirrhotic meaning affected by or relating to cirrhosis and occasionally a person with it, and noncirrhotic or non-cirrhotic; the plural is cirrhoses.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 相关术语并非完全同义：hepatic fibrosis（肝纤维化）指肝脏瘢痕组织形成，可尚未达到肝硬化阶段；chronic liver disease（慢性肝病）是更宽泛的上位概念；liver scarring（肝脏瘢痕形成）是通俗描述，不一定等于肝硬化。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: These related terms are not exact synonyms: hepatic fibrosis means liver scar formation that may not yet amount to cirrhosis; chronic liver disease is a broader category; liver scarring is a plain-language description that does not necessarily imply cirrhosis.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cirrh- 记历史上的黄褐色外观，-osis 记病变；现代核心意思是肝脏广泛瘢痕化。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link cirrh- to the historical tawny appearance and -osis to disease; the modern meaning centers on extensive liver scarring.

etymology_story.zh: dither 源于中古英语 dideren 一类表示“发抖、战栗”的词形，后来由身体颤抖发展出紧张慌乱、犹豫不决的意思。技术用法沿用了“微小扰动”的意象，指为改善量化结果而引入的细微变化。
etymology_story.en: Dither developed from Middle English forms such as dideren, meaning to tremble or shiver, and shifted from bodily trembling to nervous agitation and indecision. Its technical uses retain the idea of small disturbances introduced to improve quantization results.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 dither 是独立词基，名词和动词同形。屈折形式：dithers、dithered、dithering；派生词：ditherer（犹豫不决的人）、dithery（犹豫慌乱的，较口语化）；dithering 还可作名词，表示犹豫拖延或技术上的抖动处理。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dither is a simplex base shared by the noun and verb. Inflected forms are dithers, dithered, and dithering; derivatives include ditherer, an indecisive person, and the informal adjective dithery; dithering also functions as a noun for indecision or the technical process.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 日常义中，hesitate（犹豫）可只是短暂停顿；waver（摇摆不定）强调选择或立场来回变化；vacillate（反复犹豫）较正式，强调在不同选项之间反复摇摆。dither 通常带有不耐烦或批评色彩，突出迟迟不采取行动。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In everyday use, hesitate may describe only a brief pause; waver emphasizes an unstable choice or position; vacillate is more formal and stresses repeated movement between alternatives. Dither often conveys impatience or criticism because someone fails to act.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“发抖”记到“拿不定主意”：身体微微摇，决定也跟着摇；技术义则是加入微小扰动。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with trembling: a wavering body suggests a wavering decision, while the technical meaning involves tiny added disturbances.

etymology_story.zh: porpoise 经中古英语、盎格鲁法语传入，最终可追溯到由拉丁语 porcus（猪）和 piscis（鱼）组成、意为“猪鱼”的名称。动物名后来转作动词，用来描写海中连续跃游以及类似的机械俯仰动作。
etymology_story.en: Porpoise entered through Middle English and Anglo-French, ultimately deriving from a name combining Latin porcus, meaning pig, and piscis, meaning fish. The animal name later became a verb for repeated leaping in water and comparable pitching movements in machines.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 porpoise 是不可按现有词缀有效拆分的独立词基，名词通过零派生转作动词。词族与形式：porpoises（复数或动词第三人称单数）、porpoised（过去式及过去分词）、porpoising（现在分词；也作名词，表示跃游或反复俯仰）、porpoise-like（像鼠海豚的）；历史上的“猪＋鱼”不属于现代英语构词拆分。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, porpoise is a simplex base, with the verb formed from the noun by conversion. Forms and related words include porpoises, porpoised, porpoising as a participle or noun for leaping or pitching, and porpoise-like; the historical pig-plus-fish formation is not a modern English morphological breakdown.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 动物义没有常用的严格同义词：dolphin（海豚）是外形相似但分类不同的动物；cetacean（鲸类动物）是包含鼠海豚的上位词。机械运动义可与 pitch（俯仰）比较，但 porpoise 更强调反复发生的上下摆动或弹跳。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The animal sense has no common exact synonym: dolphin names a similar but taxonomically different animal, while cetacean is the broader category containing porpoises. For mechanical movement, pitch is related, but porpoise specifically emphasizes repeated rising, falling, or bouncing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史“猪鱼”对应短钝口鼻；再把动物跃游的起伏动作连到动词“反复俯仰”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The historical pig-fish image anchors the blunt snout; the animal's rising and falling motion anchors the verb.

morphology.text: holo-（全部） + -caust（烧毁） → holocaust（原指完全焚烧，后指大规模毁灭）。

etymology.text: 中古英语借自晚期拉丁语，源头是希腊语 holokauston（完全烧掉的祭品），后来扩展到造成巨大伤亡的浩劫。

usage_note: 本课学普通名词的浩劫义。指纳粹对犹太人等群体的大屠杀时写 the Holocaust，首字母大写；不要把它用于轻微损失。

etymology_story.zh: holocaust 经法语和拉丁语传入英语，最终源于希腊语 holokauston，指“完全焚烧的祭品”，其中 holos 表示“全部”，kaustos 表示“烧过的”。词义后来扩展为大规模毁灭；大写并通常带定冠词的 the Holocaust 成为纳粹对欧洲犹太人实施种族灭绝的历史专名。
etymology_story.en: Holocaust entered English through French and Latin from Greek holokauston, meaning a wholly burnt offering, formed from holos, meaning whole, and kaustos, meaning burnt. Its meaning broadened to mass destruction, while the capitalized expression the Holocaust became the historical name for the Nazi genocide of European Jews.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词为 holo-（全部）+ -caust（焚烧）；现代英语通常把 holocaust 作为完整名词使用，-caust 不是常见的能产后缀。核心形式为 holocaust、holocausts；Holocaust 是专名形式，Holocaust-related（与纳粹大屠杀有关的）是复合形容词；caustic、cauterize 与其焚烧成分有词源联系，但不是由 holocaust 派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: The historical formation is holo-, meaning whole, plus -caust, referring to burning; modern English generally treats holocaust as a whole noun, and -caust is not a commonly productive suffix. Core forms are holocaust and holocausts; Holocaust is the proper-name form, and Holocaust-related is a compound adjective; caustic and cauterize are etymological relatives of the burning element rather than derivatives of holocaust.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 一般义中，catastrophe（重大灾难）范围较广，不一定涉及大量死亡；massacre（大屠杀）强调对许多人的杀戮，常涉及无力反抗者；genocide（种族灭绝）强调蓄意摧毁某一民族、族裔、种族或宗教群体。the Holocaust 是特定历史事件的名称，不能随意用这些普通名词替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the general sense, catastrophe is broader and need not involve mass death; massacre emphasizes the killing of many people, often defenseless victims; genocide emphasizes the intent to destroy a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group. The Holocaust names a specific historical event and is not freely interchangeable with these general nouns.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: holo- 是“全部”，历史上的“全部烧尽”引出“毁灭性浩劫”；看到 the Holocaust，联想到特定的纳粹大屠杀历史。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Holo- means whole: the historical idea of complete burning leads to overwhelming destruction; the Holocaust names the specific Nazi genocide.

meaning: 黑色犯罪作品；黑色电影

etymology_story.zh: Noir 借自法语 noir，意为“黑色的”，该词最终源自拉丁语 niger“黑的”。英语中的文学、电影用法与 film noir“黑色电影”密切相关，后来扩展到具有相似阴暗气氛和悲观世界观的犯罪作品。
etymology_story.en: Noir comes from French noir, meaning “black,” ultimately from Latin niger. Its English literary and cinematic uses are closely associated with film noir, literally “black film,” and extended to crime works sharing its darkness and pessimism.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 noir 是不可进一步分析的借入词干，并非英语前缀与词根的组合。主要词族与构词形式：noir + -ish → noirish（带黑色犯罪作品风格的）；neo- + noir → neo-noir（新黑色电影或其风格）；noir + -esque → noiresque（具有黑色电影特色的，较少见）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, noir is an unanalyzed borrowed base, rather than a combination of English prefixes and roots. Principal family forms are noir + -ish → noirish, having noir characteristics; neo- + noir → neo-noir, a modern development of noir; and noir + -esque → noiresque, a less common adjective meaning noir-like.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: crime fiction（犯罪小说）范围更广，不必具有阴暗、悲观的世界观；hard-boiled（冷硬派的）强调强硬人物和简洁、不煽情的叙述；neo-noir（新黑色电影或作品）指对经典 noir 主题和风格的现代延续或改造。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Crime fiction is broader and need not share noir's pessimistic outlook; hard-boiled emphasizes tough characters and an unsentimental narrative style; neo-noir specifically updates or reworks the themes and techniques of classic noir.

etymology_story.zh: Retrograde 经法语和拉丁语进入中古英语，源于拉丁语 retrogradus“向后走的”，与 retro“向后”和 gradi“行走”有关。“向后移动”的本义后来引申为发展、思想或政策上的倒退。
etymology_story.en: Retrograde entered Middle English through French and Latin, from Latin retrogradus, meaning “going backward,” related to retro, “backward,” and gradi, “to step.” Physical backward movement subsequently provided a metaphor for decline in development, ideas, or policy.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 retro-（向后）+ -grade（表示行走或运动方向的拉丁语源成分）。主要词族：retrogrades、retrograded、retrograding（动词屈折形式），retrogradation（逆行；倒退），retrogradely（逆向地，少见）；retrogression（退步）和 retrogressive（倒退的）是同源相关词，并非直接在 retrograde 后加后缀形成。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be analyzed as retro-, “backward,” + -grade, a Latin-derived element referring to stepping or movement. Principal family forms include retrogrades, retrograded, retrograding, retrogradation, and the uncommon adverb retrogradely; retrogression and retrogressive are related formations from the same Latin word family rather than simple suffix additions to retrograde.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: backward（向后的）主要描述方向，也可表示落后；regressive（退步的）强调回到较差的发展阶段；retrogressive（倒退的）与评价性 retrograde 最接近，但更明确突出退步过程。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Backward primarily describes direction and can also suggest lack of development; regressive emphasizes a return to a less advanced condition; retrogressive closely matches evaluative retrograde but more explicitly emphasizes the process of decline.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: retro- 向后 + 行走 → 天体逆着走，发展往回退。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Backward + stepping → a planet moves in reverse, or progress takes a backward step.

etymology.text: 中古英语经法语、意大利语和阿拉伯语借入，最终可追到希腊语 keration（角豆种子、小重量单位）。种子曾与称重相联系，帮助记住它是重量单位。
